title: JSLH Grade 7 Mathematics Term 3 Revision Draft
contentStatus: draft; partial set; not connected to learner-centre production bank
sourceBasis: Original JSLH questions aligned to the Grade 7 2027 Mathematics Term 3 scheme: solid shapes; data collection and representation; mean, median and mode; chance and simple probability; money and budgeting.
mcq: How many faces does a cube have?
A cube has six square faces.
How many edges does a cuboid have?
A cuboid has 12 edges, where its faces meet.
Which solid has one circular base and one curved surface ending at a vertex?
A cone has one circular base and one vertex.
A solid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Which solid is it?
A square-based pyramid has one square base and four triangular faces, eight edges and five vertices.
Which graph is most suitable for comparing the number of learners in different clubs?
A bar graph compares quantities across distinct categories.
The numbers 4, 6, 6, 8 and 11 have a mean of:
Arrange the values 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; the middle value is 5.
Four occurs three times, more often than any other value.
A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of getting a 3?
There is one favourable outcome among six equally likely outcomes.
A bag contains 3 red balls and 2 blue balls. What is the probability of selecting a blue ball at random?
There are 2 blue balls out of 5 balls in total.
Which event is certain when a standard six-sided die is rolled?
A standard die has faces numbered 1 through 6.
A learner has KSh 500 and spends KSh 185. How much remains?
A family budgets KSh 1,200 for food and spends KSh 950. What fraction of the budget remains?
The remainder is 250; 250/1 200 = 5/24, so the options need checking.
A bar graph shows 12 learners chose football, 8 chose netball and 5 chose athletics. How many learners were surveyed?
A trader buys an item for KSh 240 and sells it for KSh 300. What is the profit?
Profit = selling price − cost price = 300 − 240 = KSh 60.
structured: A cuboid measures 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm. State the number of faces, edges and vertices it has.
A learner records the number of books read by five classmates as 2, 4, 3, 4 and 7. Find the mean, median and mode.
Mean = (2+4+3+4+7) ÷ 5 = 4 (2); ordered data 2,3,4,4,7 gives median 4 (1); mode 4 (1).
The marks scored by six learners are 5, 8, 6, 9, 7 and 7. Arrange the data in ascending order and find the median.
Ascending order: 5,6,7,7,8,9 (2); median is average of 3rd and 4th values = (7+7) ÷ 2 = 7 (2).
A bag contains 4 green counters, 3 yellow counters and 5 red counters. Find the probability of selecting (a) a yellow counter and (b) a counter that is not red.
Total counters = 12 (1); P(yellow) = 3/12 = 1/4 (1); not red = 4+3=7 counters (1); P(not red)=7/12 (1).
A class survey found that 14 learners prefer football, 9 prefer volleyball and 7 prefer athletics. Present the information in a frequency table and state the total number surveyed.
Correct headings/categories (1); football 14 (1); volleyball 9 (1); athletics 7 and total 30 (1).
A learner receives KSh 1,500 pocket money for a week. The budget is KSh 600 for food, KSh 350 for transport and KSh 250 for saving. Calculate the total allocated and the unallocated balance.
A trader buys 20 exercise books at KSh 35 each and sells each at KSh 42. Calculate the total cost, total sales and profit.
Explain two reasons why a household should prepare a budget and give two practices that can help it follow the budget.
One mark each for two valid reasons such as controlling spending or prioritising needs (2); one mark each for two practical practices such as recording expenses or comparing prices (2).
